bibliographic.title: Review Chatbot for Health Care and Oncology Applications Using Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning: Systematic Review
bibliographic.authors: Lu Xu; Leslie Sanders; Kay Li; James C L Chow
bibliographic.citation_apa: Xu, L., Sanders, L., Li, K., & Chow, J. C. L. (2021). Review chatbot for health care and oncology applications using artificial intelligence and machine learning: Systematic review. JMIR Cancer, 7(4), e27850. https://doi.org/10.2196/27850

methodology.study_design: systematic review with database search (IEEE Xplore, PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, OVID) for studies from 2000 to 2020, screening guided by Botlist directory and categorized by diagnosis, treatment, monitoring, support, workflow, and health promotion
methodology.sample_description: chatbots in health care and oncology applications identified through literature search and Botlist directory
methodology.technology_context: chatbots; conversational agents; artificial intelligence; machine learning; deep learning; healthcare applications

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a 2021 systematic review of chatbots in health care and oncology using AI/ML, covering literature from 2000-2020. It addresses regulated healthcare contexts and mentions ethical, security, technical, and regulatory standards, but the provided text does not address LLM-based systems or conversational governance mechanisms such as guardrails, observability, accountability frameworks, or operational governance. It offers contextual background rather than central evidence for LLM conversational governance.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Extracted metadata appears corrupted (title/venue mismatch with PDF front matter); full-text eligibility and governance relevance require human verification beyond partial excerpts.

appraisal.notes: Clear systematic review objective and search strategy are described, but only partial methods/results are available in the provided text; appraisal is limited to visible signals.

cerqual.explanation: The review appears methodologically structured with defined databases and search terms, but available excerpts do not provide full screening, appraisal, or synthesis detail. Relevance to LLM conversational governance is indirect: useful for regulated healthcare chatbot context and concern areas, not for LLM-specific governance mechanisms.

coding.theme: chatbot applications and concerns in regulated health care
coding.subtheme: oncology and cancer therapy chatbot use cases

synthesis.main_claim: Chatbots using AI/ML show promise for health care and oncology applications, but human elements remain non-replaceable; ethical, security, technical, and regulatory issues explain implementation hesitancy.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a systematic review of recent advances and trends in medical chatbot technology with emphasis on cancer therapy applications and categorized use cases.
synthesis.limitations: The provided text highlights limitations and areas of concern around ethical, moral, security, technical, and regulatory standards and evaluation issues; broader review limitations are unclear from excerpts.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational/contextual evidence on healthcare chatbots in regulated settings and high-level ethical/regulatory concerns; not primary evidence for LLM-based conversational governance frameworks.
